data.title: Review minors batch: watch/reload startup races + suppression window; date min/max author UX; conflict-shape consistency

fields.description:
Batch of small correctness/polish items from the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) — reload/watch startup + config authoring UX. Each is a contained fix; land as one branch of small commits.

RELOAD/WATCH (flagged independently by two reviewers):
1) setAfterReload ordering race: cmd/cards/serve.go:126 starts the watcher before setAfterReload at :160; plain field write (reload.go:81-83) read by notifyReload — no happens-before. Failure: missed service reconcile on a first-tick reload under --watch --run-extensions. FIX: install before spawning the watcher (one-line move) or make the field atomic.
2) Watcher not awaited on shutdown: watchCancel deferred but Run not joined (contrast supervisor's supDone, serve.go:163-173); SIGINT during scanOnce can race reloadLocked against store close. FIX: done channel like the supervisor's.
3) Self-write suppression window swallows a concurrent external edit: while selfWriteGate.active>0, scanOnce absorbs ANY fingerprint and advances lastFP (watch.go:114-118) — an external save during the create-board handler window is silently dropped until the next change. FIX: during active window skip WITHOUT advancing lastFP; only skipFP should advance it.
4) Stale skipFP can absorb a later legitimate change (watch.go:207-211): cleared only on match; if the first post-create observation differs, it lingers and can swallow an exact-revert later. FIX: one-tick TTL.

7) Store-level version_conflict returns the ATTEMPTED card, not current DB state (internal/sqlite/sqlite.go:587-588) — matters for the versionless MCP tools under a genuine race. Pre-existing; fix while nearby.
8) RemoveEntry rejects version 0 as validation error while AppendEntry/UpdateEntry treat omitted version as version_conflict — inconsistent shape; pick one.

data.title: Core/HTTP: card delete (DELETE /v1/cards/:id + tombstone event + idempotency)

fields.description:
Add a first-class card-delete path so junk/test/superseded cards can be hard-removed instead of being closed-as-done with a comment (the current workaround used during the 2026-07 board cleanup, which hit exactly this gap).

Scope:
- DELETE /v1/cards/:id HTTP route (mirror existing PATCH auth/actor/idempotency: X-Work-Cards-Actor header, Idempotency-Key, optimistic version in ?version= query param).
- CLI: `cards delete <id> --version N` (serverless + HTTP, like patch/claim).
- MCP: a `delete_card` tool (the MCP tool list currently has no delete either).
- Core: Service.RemoveCard(id, version, actor) — atomic. Emit a new `card_removed` durable event (typed constructor in internal/core/events.go per EVENTS.md §4 no-raw-literals rule) carrying the removed card's id/type/title snapshot in Diff for replay/audit. Persist via the existing commitCard seam (or the ClaimAtomic-style atomic path if no card row update is needed — decide and document).
- Safety: delete is a hard, irreversible mutation. Require the current version (optimistic concurrency) so a stale client cannot delete a card that changed underneath it. Consider a workspace setting to soft-delete (tombstone) vs hard-delete; default to hard-delete + event to match append-only audit design. Refusing to delete a card that still has inbound links is an open question — propose: reject with 409 if any inbound links exist (caller removes links first), OR cascade-remove the card's links but refuse to cascade across cards. Pick one and document in SPEC.md §11.
- Docs: SPEC.md §11 (add the route), §8 (add card_removed to the event catalog + diff shape), INTEGRATOR-REFERENCE.md §2/§4, MCP.md (tool table), DEVELOPER-REFERENCE.md §9 (CLI). Status: [proposed].

Out of scope: bulk delete, undo/recycle, retention windows.

Acceptance:
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` green with new tests covering: delete by current version succeeds and emits card_removed; stale version returns 409 version_conflict; delete is idempotent under a replayed Idempotency-Key (returns the original 204/200); deleting a card with inbound links behaves per the chosen policy with a test.
- OpenAPI spec (internal/openapi) updated; `cards delete` works in both serverless and HTTP modes; MCP `delete_card` tool listed and working.

data.title: Sprint 07-11 P5b: supervise kind:service — listener-ready gate, crash-loop backoff with min-healthy-uptime, bounded drain

fields.description:
Phase 5 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-11.md. Audience: the extension developer — judged on 'an external process I wrote in any language survives crashes and consumes events'. Turns extensions-over-plugins into working mechanism.

DO — the supervised-process class with real lifecycle semantics:
1) Listener-ready gate: start services only after the net.Listener is accepting (create the listener before the supervisor goroutine, or pass a readiness channel); hand each child the loopback base URL via env so 'how does the service find the server' is defined, not assumed.
2) Bounded backoff WITH a minimum-healthy-uptime threshold before the counter resets — a runs-briefly-then-crashes service escalates to the cap instead of pinning CPU. Crash-loop test REQUIRED.
3) Bounded drain: SIGTERM, configurable grace period, then SIGKILL the process group (reuse hooks.go's procgroup fallback). A SIGTERM-ignoring child must be force-killed within the grace window — test REQUIRED. Shutdown always returns.
4) ONE shared supervisor-construction path used by both serve --run-extensions (serve.go:130) and standalone run-extensions (extensions.go:56); the ADR names serve --run-extensions as the supported home.

Budget explicitly for mac+linux race-clean signal tests (fake crashing/hanging child binaries) — the existing procgroup_unix/other split shows this does not come free.

FALLBACK if P2/P3 slip badly: ship supervisor-without-reconcile (services restart on every reload, documented) rather than slipping the whole north star.

ACCEPTANCE: kind:service autostarts after the listener accepts; restarts per policy without crash-loop CPU pinning; hung child force-killed within grace; both entry points share one wiring; go test ./... green and race-clean on mac+linux.

data.title: Events seam 3d: deadline min-heap scheduler for temporal conditions (status_timeout, card_idle)

fields.description: docs/EVENTS.md §11.2; design already refined in INTEGRATION.md comments (deadline min-heap, no fixed tick, sleeps until earliest deadline, empty heap = no wakeups). This is the hardest and riskiest piece of the condition-event system — land it as its own isolated slice, after the instant-condition machinery (3a-3c) has already validated Signal/Emit/persist:true. Deadlines armed from a denormalized status_since column + a fired-marker keyed by (card,status,status_since); reconstructible from state, nothing persisted for scheduling itself. Lazy/refcounted: only scheduled while a monitor has a live consumer (SSE filter, hook/webhook, or persist:true), dropped when the last consumer disconnects. Acceptance: unit-testable scheduler with an injected clock (no real sleeps in tests); zero-wakeup idle test (empty heap does not spin); refcount test (deadline dropped when last consumer disconnects, re-armed on reconnect); crossing-state idempotency test.

fields.acceptance: Tests: happy path (200 with valid bearer); 401 on missing/invalid/unknown token (identical generic body — no enumeration); constant-time compare unit test; CRITICAL anti-spoof test: valid bearer + mismatched X-Work-Cards-Actor commits with the AUTHENTICATED actor (assert on the event's actor field); forced write without credentials → 401; --auth none regression: existing httpapi tests pass unchanged; identity-before-idempotency: same Idempotency-Key under two different tokens creates two distinct writes. fields.description:
Reference implementation of docs/design/AUTH.md (frozen 2026-07-10 — the doc is normative for this card; see docs/NOTES.md freeze entry). Backlog until the AUTH.md review lands (card_61040a3e); promotes to todo then.

BEHAVIOR (AUTH.md §§1-4):
- cards serve --auth <none|token> (proxy mode is a LATER slice, not this card).
- POST /v1/users issues an opaque high-entropy bearer token, shown once. DB stores hash only (constant-time compare via crypto/subtle). No GET-token endpoint. Rotate = revoke + reissue (cards users token rotate <id>).
- Writes under --auth token require Authorization: Bearer; actor = the registered User.ID the token maps to. Reads stay open in v0 (host ACL is the read confidentiality line; --auth-require-read is future work).
- Under --auth none: today's behavior exactly — ambient hints (X-Work-Cards-Actor → CARDS_USER → DefaultUser), actor may be an unregistered free string, Kind best-effort. DefaultUser is NOT consulted under token.
- Bootstrap: serverless CLI register always trusted; HTTP POST /v1/users under token gated by an existing valid bearer (v0 stopgap: first CLI-registered user is the admin bit). --save writes ~/.cards/credentials; CARDS_TOKEN env supported (MCP adapter binds identity at process spawn).
- Identity resolves BEFORE idempotency replay (AUTH.md §5 — keys are per-actor).
- 401 for ALL failure modes; no user enumeration; rate-silenced failure logs; NEVER log token material.
- Force never bypasses auth: forced writes still 401 without valid credentials.

NOT THIS CARD: proxy mode, --auth-require-read, sessions/cookies (reference-client pattern — the web UI may store the bearer client-side; that is a separate thin follow-on spike), Basic-auth adapter (optional later: Basic maps user:token onto the same store — one-line mention in AUTH.md §11, do NOT implement in v0), scoped tokens, groups semantics.

BIND WARN INTERACTION: pairs with card_fa239a92 — non-loopback + auth=none gets the extra remediation line; non-loopback + auth=token gets the single WARN only.

data.title: Sprint 07-12 P3: reader pool (or write-hold reduction), proven on file+WAL — CANONICAL read-pool card

fields.description:
Phase 3 of docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-12.md — CANONICAL read-pool card (reconciled from the duplicate sprawl in P1c; staged-plan evidence lives on the closed planning card card_fec18019). Ship whichever concurrency fix P2b's measurement selected — the sprint does not collapse to hygiene.

PRIMARY SCOPE (P2b verdict a): a reader pool so reads stop queueing behind the single writer.
1) Split Open into two handles: writer keeps the current DSN (_txlock=immediate, MaxOpenConns(1)); reader pool gets a DSN WITHOUT _txlock=immediate, opened read-only (mode=ro or query_only) so a misrouted write fails loudly. Sequence: open writer → Ping → Init/migrate (establishes WAL) → THEN construct the reader pool with matching busy_timeout/foreign_keys. Pool-size knob (env/config); size 1 restores today's serialized behavior (runtime escape hatch). Centralize pragma construction (two DSNs = pragma-drift risk). core.Store doc comment: migrations writer-only; readers see last committed WAL snapshot; read-your-own-writes needs the writer; cross-process immediate-tx discipline unchanged.
2) COMPLETE audit table — every Store method in exactly one column (exit criterion). Readers on pool: ListCards, CountCards, GetCard, GetCardsByShortID, ListLinks, AllLinks, Blockers, BlockingDependents, ListComments, comment counts, EventQuery List/Page, ListUsers, + advisory check-then-act reads ConditionFired (sqlite.go:~1050) and GetIdempotency (sqlite.go:~1137) — safe on pool ONLY because the authoritative guard is the in-tx INSERT-OR-IGNORE rowcount / writer-side upsert (note this). Writer: Insert/Update/DeleteCard, ClaimAtomic, link/comment writes, event Append, idempotency writes, user upserts, migrations. Audit SEQUENCES: any write-then-reread-to-render path reads through the writer; give reader helpers a queryer interface (pool or tx) so query code isn't forked. Note: UpdateCard's conflict re-read inside its own immediate tx makes a stale pool GetCard yield a normal version_conflict — no new hazard.
3) Prove on file+WAL (not memory): (i) regression test, tempdir WAL, N readers return while a writer holds the write lock, race-clean; (ii) freshness test — create a card through the normal handler path, immediately re-read, assert fresh version; (iii) re-run the P2b benchmark for after-numbers.

data.title: Supervisor hardening: WaitDelay on service children, bounded log sink, startup dup race

fields.description:
From the sprint 07-11 post-merge review (b23aff8) of the P5 service supervisor. Two production-hang/memory risks plus two small races — all targeted fixes in the existing structure.

1) MAJOR — no cmd.WaitDelay on service children: runServiceOnce (internal/hooks/services.go:167-230) pipes stdout/stderr but never sets cmd.WaitDelay; the hook path sets 5s at hooks.go:226 for exactly this. A service that daemonizes a setsid grandchild inheriting stdout makes cmd.Wait block forever after SIGKILL (pgroup miss): the unbounded <-done at services.go:267 means cards serve never exits on Ctrl-C, and the same hang in stopOne (reconcile.go:175) wedges reconcileMu — every later reload/board-create HTTP handler blocks. FIX: set WaitDelay on service cmds and/or bound the post-SIGKILL <-done.

2) MAJOR — unbounded memory for chatty services: services.go:186-188 accumulates the child's entire stdout/stderr in bytes.Buffers, flushed to .cards/logs/<id>.log only at exit. Long-running services grow supervisor RSS without bound. FIX: bounded ring buffer or streaming file sink (hooks stay as-is — one-shot buffering is fine there).

3) MINOR race — duplicate supervised children at startup: Run publishes s.svcCtx (hooks.go:130) before startAutostartServices takes reconcileMu (services.go:91); a reload in that window has Reconcile start every autostart service, then startAutostartServices startOnes them all again (no already-managed check, services.go:93-96) — two supervised copies of the same id, permanently. FIX: assign svcCtx under reconcileMu, or make startOne skip ids already in s.services.

4) MINOR test flake (observed once under -race): TestReconcileAddedStarts — waitServicePID returns at pid registration, which can precede bash writing the marker; stat-once then fails. FIX: poll for the marker.

VERIFY: go test -race ./internal/hooks ./cmd/cards; new test for a SIGTERM-ignoring child with an out-of-pgroup descendant holding stdout returning within grace+WaitDelay.

data.title: Bug: board filter stalls after several rapid changes (SSE connection churn)

fields.description:
REPORTED (review): changing a board's Type filter several times in a row makes filtering stop responding; further filter changes have no effect until, after some seconds, the backend 'recovers' and the board finally updates.

DIAGNOSIS (root cause, code-verified):
- Board filter controls (Owner/Type/Sort) do a FULL-PAGE GET navigation (board.html: select onchange='this.form.submit()'). Every page load opens a NEW EventSource to /v1/events/stream (board.html SSE script).
- The SSE handler (internal/httpapi/sse.go) cleans up correctly on ctx.Done(), BUT the browser does not tear down the old EventSource instantly on navigation, and the server only notices a dead SSE connection on its next write. With HTTP/1.1's ~6-connections-per-host limit, a handful of rapid filter navigations saturate the connection pool with half-dead SSE streams, so the next navigation's requests block until an old connection is reaped -> 'recovers after time'.
- Aggravated by two things: (a) SQLite SetMaxOpenConns(1) serializes every board render through one connection; (b) the board SSE script re-fetches the WHOLE board (fetch(window.location.href)) on EVERY event, so event bursts pile DB-bound requests on top of the filter navigations.

FIX OPTIONS (cheap -> structural):
1. SSE heartbeat: emit ': keepalive' every ~15-20s so a write to a dead connection fails fast, the handler returns + unsubscribes, and the slot frees promptly (directly shrinks 'recovers after time'). Cheapest, high value.
2. Stop the connection churn: make filter changes an htmx partial swap (hx-get -> swap #board) instead of full-page nav, so ONE SSE connection persists across filter changes.
3. Debounce/coalesce the SSE-driven full-board refetch so event bursts don't stack DB-bound requests.
4. SQLite read pool (see card_fec1801913 / ROADMAP §3) removes the single-connection serialization.

Recommend 1+3 first (small, safe), then 2. Acceptance: rapidly change the Type filter 10x in a row -> the board keeps updating with no multi-second stall; SSE connections do not accumulate (verify server logs / netstat).

comments.author: jeremy
comments.body: FIXED in rebuild Phase 9 (commit 1af2dc2, card card_93ef776d57004034a50ee8057e2be4ae). Root causes addressed: (a) the persistent EventSource is now decoupled from filter navigation — $store.live is ONE connection for the page lifetime; filter changes fragment-swap the board via X-Cards-Partial without touching SSE. Verified: 20 rapid filter changes → same EventSource instance, status stays open. (b) Server-side keepalive as a ticker case in the SAME single-writer for/select (~20s ':keepalive'): a dead peer fails fast on the next write, freeing the bus slot promptly and shrinking the 'recovers after time' tail. Pinned by TestSSEKeepalive. Also delivered: reactive drag-drop, board_fragment partial, debounced swapBoard on live events, exponential-backoff reconnect with ?since=<lastId>.

data.title: Design: user-defined columns/card-types — how far does the UI go?

fields.description:
QUESTION (review): when creating a board, columns and card types look fixed. Are they user-definable (CLI/web), and how far do we take the UI — visual schema editing, or just files?

CURRENT STATE (code-verified):
- Columns and card types ARE user-defined — at the WORKSPACE level, in git-backed files: workspace.json 'columns', and definitions/card-types/<id>.json. Boards reference SUBSETS.
- The create-board modal (board_create.html) intentionally offers CHECKBOXES of EXISTING workspace columns + existing card types; validateBoard enforces board.columns subset-of workspace.columns and card_type_ids reference existing types. That's why they look 'fixed' — a board composes existing building blocks, it can't invent columns/types inline.
- Adding a NEW column = edit workspace.json; a NEW card type = add a card-types/*.json file; then reload. No UI for that yet. (create-a-board already WRITES a reviewable definitions/boards/<id>.json — the 'UI writes files' pattern.)

DIRECTION (per PHILOSOPHY.md #2 Files-where-they-help, #3 Schemas-not-magic, #6 Extensions-over-plugins):
- Schemas stay explicit, versioned, git-backed FILES. The UI's job is to WRITE/EDIT those files (as create-a-board does), not to become the source of truth.

data.title: Core/CLI: serverless CLI — auto-select backend (direct core+sqlite vs HTTP)

fields.description:
Let read/write CLI commands work without a running HTTP server, in addition to (not instead of) the server.

Already partly true: the transport-agnostic core (internal/core) is shared by all surfaces, and export/import/mcp already skip HTTP — they call sqlite.Open + core.NewService directly against the workspace DB. Extending list/get/create/patch/... to do the same is mostly wiring.

Why: zero-config one-shots (`cards list` in a .cards/ dir just works, matching the new git-style workspace resolution); lower latency; no port/URL bookkeeping.

Two catches that mean HTTP cannot simply be dropped: (1) the event bus is in-process — a CLI writing directly to the DB bypasses a running server bus, so SSE live updates and status_changed hooks would not fire; (2) SQLite is single-writer across processes — direct writes while `cards serve` holds the DB risk SQLITE_BUSY/lock contention (WAL allows concurrent readers).

Clean design (matches ARCHITECTURE notes): CLI auto-selects its backend — if CARDS_URL is set or a server is detected, use HTTP so events/hooks/SSE stay correct; otherwise open core+sqlite directly for a fast serverless one-shot. Cost: a small backend interface the CLI commands target, with HTTP and direct-service implementations behind it.

work_log.notes: Implemented via a cli.Transport seam: in-process backend runs the real /v1 router (httptest) against the resolved workspace; HTTP backend used when CARDS_URL set. No CARDS_URL => serverless. Reuses full handler/service stack, zero duplication. Tested + e2e verified.

data.title: Sprint 2026-07-12: concurrent reads on an honest ledger (tracker)

fields.description:
SPRINT TRACKER — plan doc: docs/plans/sprint-2026-07-12.md. The board IS the plan: card bodies carry the executable detail; phase exits update statuses on the card IDs below.

PITCH: An internal-substrate sprint, framed honestly — no board viewer or CLI user sees a new feature. It ships (1) a planning ledger that tells the truth about code, with the recurring drift class converted into a behavior-asserting CI test, and (2) the sanctioned SQLite reader pool — OR, if measurement says reads aren't the pain, the write-hold-time reduction that is — so the multi-agent concurrency the last sprint enabled stops queueing every read behind one connection. Payoff is perceptible only under concurrent load; the closing demo is measured and felt through MCP/HTTP, not a microbenchmark table. Auth stays a frozen design decision closed out on the board, not code built here.

PHASES → CARDS:
P1a card_29200d8b93454c008818a410a70e4306 (ledger truth: date min/max shipped, coverage fix, behavior drift test)
P1b card_7a3f4ebd224946d585ce5a0c25ab2cf2 (auth closeout: ROADMAP §1 → frozen AUTH.md, close review card, park bearer impl)
P1c card_8f8cbde7281c44038ff6d4652bc01e5e (reconcile read-pool card ids to one canonical)
P2a card_77d6c663021e427ab40c2fff43d8e8a7 (shared-cache test harness: one constructor, ~29 :memory: sites)
P2b card_495d2e09de854e478b65056ae95c16ae (measured file-WAL baseline + written a/b/c verdict)
P3 card_57e1bde9bb6e467bbed771835d45a788 (reader pool OR write-hold reduction, proven on file+WAL — canonical read-pool card)

STANDING RULES: P1 is parallel bookkeeping (do it now; it is NOT the spine). P2 starts immediately, no dependency on P1. P3 scope is DECIDED BY P2b's measured verdict, not assumed — verdict (c) "park with evidence" is a success, not a failure. All measurement on file-backed WAL through a real transport (:memory: has no fsync and fakes the verdict). Two-DSN pragma construction is centralized (drift risk). Phase exits update card statuses; sprint close exports + commits the JSONL once.

OUT OF SCOPE (deliberate): AUTH reference impl (card_350b1bac — security-sensitive XL, its own sprint, never stacked with the pool) · any in-core authz/RBAC/sessions/multi-tenant (AUTH.md §11 non-goals stand) · re-implementing date min/max (already shipped; P1a is a ledger correction only) · re-writing AUTH.md (frozen c6cb17e) · release.yml actions bump (verified false premise — already on @v4) · a user-visible feature added just to give the sprint a demo (scope creep on an infra sprint) · Postgres/alt backends (deferred until this WAL optimization is proven) · /ui/definitions read-only view (needs its own investigation pass — card_8903f9aa) · outbox/tailer webhooks (parked behind OUTBOX-GONOGO).

RISKS: misclassifying a Store method/sequence as pool-safe reintroduces SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT-class failures or stale read-your-own-writes — the complete audit table + queryer interface + handler freshness test mitigate, but audit completeness IS the failure mode to watch. modernc shared-cache named-memory semantics must behave as documented — verify with a focused test BEFORE migrating 29 sites. P2b may select the alternate scope or park — a designed outcome; harness/audit/doc land regardless. The felt demo needs enough concurrent load to make the before-case visibly queue; if dogfooding-scale can't reproduce it, report honest p50/p95 and say so. Auth closeout can balloon if treated as fresh design — keep it S-sized review+crosslink. Two DSNs mean pragma drift — centralize pragma construction; reviewers check it in the diff.

data.title: Design RFC: transitions-as-callbacks + trigger seam (board-shipped behavior) — v0.5 direction

fields.description:
Planted for NEXT sprint. First-pass sketch for docs/design/BOARD-BEHAVIOR.md. GOVERNING DOCS (frozen 2026-07-10, see docs/NOTES.md freeze entry): docs/design/CORE-BOUNDARIES.md §3.3 (three-layer framing + force policy) and docs/design/AUTH.md §7 (identity invariant). OUT of sprint 07-10 (see sprint tracker card_3f225267).

THREE-LAYER FRAMING (from CORE-BOUNDARIES §3.3 — adopt in the RFC):
- DECLARATIVE GRAPH (Board.Transitions in board JSON) = core DATA, introspectable/exportable — STAYS. Same family as columns and WIP limits.
- ENFORCEMENT (service.go:751, :1456 refusal) = the seam this RFC refactors behind a Validator interface, with in-core evaluate as the builtin first chain link.
- OBSERVATION (transition_rejected, events.go:283) = stays wherever enforcement lives; continuity guaranteed.
The vision quote ('core should not have strong opinions about transitions') bans PROGRAMMABLE rules in core, not the declarative map.

OVERLAY PRINCIPLE at top of the doc:
'Core ships contracts and boring defaults. Policy richness lives at the boundary (auth adapter, validate callback, external hooks) — never as a growing in-process product dialect.'

SHAPE — data + code:
- Declared RULES (data): today's transitions: map, plus optional require_field_before etc. — read by a default builtin validator.
- Optional per-board VALIDATOR (subprocess declared in board JSON) returning a narrow verdict.
- Default = current EnforceTransitions behavior refactored behind the interface, so nothing regresses.

RUNTIME, DECIDED: SUBPROCESS-FIRST, single implementation. Embedded JS is EXPLICIT NON-GOAL until someone shows a demo subprocess can't carry. No behavior.js implicit paths — the board JSON declares a command.

BOARD DECLARATION (example):
  "behavior": { "validate": { "command": ["./extensions/eng-validate"], "timeout_ms": 200 } }

VERDICT WIRE SHAPE (JSON stdout of the subprocess):
  { "allow": true, "code": "transition_illegal", "message": "...",
    "field": "status", "valid_options": ["review"] }
Reuses existing structured-error vocabulary; no partial card mutations; no nested Service calls; max stdout size (documented).

FAIL-CLOSED MATRIX (writes only; reads never call this):
- timeout → fail-closed
- non-zero exit or unparseable JSON → fail-closed
- allow:false without a code → default transition_illegal (transitions) / validation_error (field triggers)
- subprocess missing / not executable → fail-closed with a CLEAR OPERATOR MESSAGE (config error, not a validation event)

CONTINUITY OF OBSERVATION: builtin deny and callback deny share the existing transition_rejected event/code path (events.go:283 already emits this today). Add an optional diff.source = "builtin" | "board_validate" only if it earns its keep in debugging — no new public event surface in v1.

EVENT COVERAGE, PHASED (avoids the workflow-engine siren):
- v1: status transitions only (patch/create status) — replaces in-core enforce.
- v1.1: declarative require_field_before_transition — ONE PATTERN ONLY ('status S requires field F set'), not a rules language. Compiles to the same Validator interface as the default builtin, so board subprocesses sit as chain peers, not special cases.
- v2: on_comment_added / on_field_changed validators ONLY IF real demand.

CHAIN ORDER: builtin declarative rules → board callback → commit. The callback does not reimplement column membership unless the operator opts into 'disable builtin.'

FORCE POLICY (decided 2026-07-10, CORE-BOUNDARIES §3.3 revised — this card is its durable home):
- Force is a PER-WRITE request field (force:true in PATCH body / req.Force / CLI --force), not a serve mode.
- force=true SKIPS BOTH the builtin declarative rules AND the board-callback validator — matches today's req.Force behavior; the web UI's drag-and-force-confirm flow depends on it. YOLO escape hatch by default.
- Force NEVER skips identity verification: under --auth token/proxy an unauthenticated forced write is 401 (AUTH.md §7). Attribution of a forced write is the resolved verified identity.
- NO NEW EVENT TYPE: forced-ness rides status_changed with diff.forced=true. A separate transition_forced EventType was considered and rejected (SPEC + bus-filter + INTEGRATOR churn without consumer demand).
- BOARD OPT-OUT: settings.allow_force:false makes the declarative graph a hard floor for that board (no force override there). Data, not code — same family as enforce_transitions. Small SPEC-DATA-MODEL addition.

HOOKS / VALIDATORS COVENANT (the load-bearing distinction — PHILOSOPHY §5 boundary):

| Seam                | Timing                      | Power                    | Contract |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------|----------|
| Hooks (today)       | post-commit, at-most-once   | observe / side effects   | no veto |
| Validators (proposed)| pre-commit, sync, bounded  | verdict only             | no email/HTTP/card writes from the sandbox; if a validator does that via its own subprocess, that's the operator's problem — core provides no client helpers |

MIGRATION STORY: boards with today's enforce_transitions: true and no custom behavior → IDENTICAL outcomes; transition_rejected event still fires; no observable regression.

OPEN TENSIONS (decided next sprint, not now):
- Validator sync cost on every write: queue depth, panic isolation, dry-run escape hatch.
- Definition-trust ≠ card-ACL: see AUTH.md implementation notes.

data.title: Reconsider RemoveEntry CAS: HTTP DELETE passes version=0, skipping concurrency guard

fields.description: Service.RemoveEntry treats version==0 as 'no CAS' (skip the version check), and the HTTP DELETE handler passes 0 unconditionally. Decide and implement/test accordingly.
